blocks: Press Tie/Rest without holding notes to insert a silent step and advance.
To sustain a note or chord across steps, hold it and press Tie/Rest for each additional step. Releasing the keys advances again.
The display shows the current step and its recorded notes. After the final step, the MicroFreak enters Play mode automatically.
In step recording, an incoming MIDI Start/Play message switches the sequencer to real-time recording.

Select A or B, stop playback, and press Record. Turn Rate/Swing to move through the steps. The MicroFreak plays each step's notes and recorded modulation as you reach it, looping to the beginning after the final step.
At the desired step, hold new notes to replace the stored notes. Press Hold to replace the step with a rest.
Start playback, then press Record. A blinking Record icon means the sequencer is waiting for notes or knob movements.
During note recording, each pass through the loop replaces notes played at the corresponding steps in the previous pass. Modulation recording runs for one cycle and then stops recording.
Playing a note replaces the recorded note at that point. Pressing Hold while recording replaces notes or modulation events at that point with silence; you can fill the gap on the next pass.
A DAW can play notes into a MicroFreak set to real-time recording. You can later add knob movement to the modulation tracks.
Tip: A longer sequence provides finer recording resolution. Set its length in Utility > Preset > Seq Length; a slower recording rate can make note and modulation placement easier.
Hold the source pattern's A or B icon, then press the destination pattern's icon. To copy A to B, hold A and press B; to copy B to A, hold B and press A. Check the display for confirmation.
Copying a pattern lets you keep its melody while recording different modulation movements in the other pattern, then alternate between the two during performance.
13.1.3.5. Using the Arpeggiator to Create Sequences

Create an arpeggio and transfer it to a sequence to retain its Spice & Dice variations. Standard sequence recording disables Spice & Dice, so transferring an arpeggio is the way to include those effects in a sequence. See Microfreak/UG/12 Arpeggiator for the transfer procedure.

02 The Sequencer Controls Stop and Start

Each pattern has four modulation tracks. The note sequence records pitch and velocity; each modulation track records the position of one control at each step. A track can hold as many values as the sequence has steps, up to 64.
In step recording, record the notes first, then capture control positions at the desired steps. Notes and modulation can also be recorded together by holding notes while turning controls.
Select a pattern, stop playback, and press Record. Turn Rate/Swing to select the step where modulation should begin.

Turn a control to audition its value. The display shows the step, modulation slot, parameter, and amount. Release the control to store that position with the step. Move to another step with Rate/Swing and set the next value. Repeat across the pattern.
You can fill one control's track across all steps before assigning another control, or set up to four controls at each step before moving on.

Turning Rate/Swing through the steps plays their stored notes and modulation, so you can hear and edit each value. Turn its assigned control to replace a stored position. Oct | Mod cycles through active modulation tracks.
Oscillator: Type, Wave, Timbre, and Shape. With sample selection enabled, Type controls sample selection.
Envelope: Attack, Decay, Sustain, and Filter Amount.
Cycling Envelope: Rise, Fall, Hold, and Amount sent to the Matrix.
Matrix: Modulation amount of a matrix point.
To clear a track, press Oct | Mod until its light blinks, then hold Oct | Mod and press Hold. Press Hold repeatedly while holding Oct | Mod to clear further tracks.

Start Play and Record, then move a control. Recording begins at the first step that captures a movement, continues for one full loop, and stops just before that step on the next pass. Record turns off automatically.
To erase the selected modulation track, hold Oct | Mod and press Hold. Keep Oct | Mod held and press Hold again to erase each following track.

Smoothing, or slew, makes changes between stored modulation values gradual, much as Glide smooths changes in pitch. Set each track separately in Utility > Preset > Seq (X) smooth, where X is the modulation track number from 1 to 4.
A new track recorded step by step has smoothing off by default. A new track recorded in real time has smoothing on by default. Overwriting an existing track keeps its smoothing setting.
Rests and ties can give a sequence more varied rhythm. For example, a 32-step sequence with rests and ties played at double speed can be more varied than 16 filled steps at normal speed.

Patterns A and B share the effects of their modulation tracks when you switch between them. Suppose A changes oscillator type on steps one and four. If you switch to B after step four, B starts with the oscillator type last set by A; switching before step four leaves B with the type set on step one.

The sequencer controls oscillator pitch directly. Route the LFO to pitch through the Matrix as well, and the two signals add together. A slow rectangular LFO makes the sequence jump between pitch levels. Change the Matrix amount to control the size and direction of the shift.

Variation: Also route the LFO to filter cutoff. With enough modulation to close the filter, some parts of the sequence fall silent. Try different LFO waveforms and amounts to change the rhythm of those gaps.

A random LFO waveform can transpose a running sequence at unpredictable times. Change LFO speed to change when transpositions occur; increase the Matrix amount for wider jumps or use a negative amount to invert the modulation.
Hoketus keeps one pitch while changing timbre, articulation, and rhythm. On the MicroFreak, use modulation tracks to change parameters while the sequence repeats that pitch.

Create a 16-step sequence with the same pitch at every step. Add rests and ties for rhythm, then press Record while playback is stopped. Turn a control to capture its position, use Rate/Swing to move to the next step, and repeat. Up to four controls can change across the pattern.
Variation: To imitate a monochord, use one or two modulation tracks to introduce nearby pitches around the repeated central pitch.
Utility settings can change how a sequence and preset behave. Try switching Glide Mode between Time and Rate, enabling Envelope Legato, or changing smoothing on a sequencer modulation track.

Preset settings are saved with each preset, including Volume, Bend Range, and Pressure mode. Global settings apply to every preset; for example, an A reference of 441 Hz changes the tuning of all presets.
You can adjust settings on the MicroFreak in Utility or on a computer in MIDI Control Center (MCC). Preset settings are available only in Utility.
Access to the configuration setting in Utility
Utility settings fall into Preset and Global categories. The settings below indicate whether they are available on the MicroFreak in Utility and in MIDI Control Center (MCC).
These settings are saved with each preset and are available in Utility. They are unavailable in MCC.
Bend Range: 0–24 semitones; up to two octaves.
Glide Mode: Time, Sync, or Rate; controls whether the Glide knob sets glide time, tempo-synced glide, or glide rate.
Unison Spread: 0.001–12.000; spread between the four voices.
Unison Count: 2–4 voices in unison mode.
Envelope Legato: Off or On; controls envelope reset on a keyboard trigger.
Envelope Snap: Off or On; sharpens the envelope decay.
LFO Retrig: Off, On, or Legato; controls retriggering on keyboard triggers and during legato playing.
Press Mode: Aftertouch or Velocity; selects the pressure mode.
Key/Arp Mode: Linear or Random; Random generates a new random value for each key pressed.
Velo Amp Mod: 0–10; controls how much velocity affects output volume.
Preset Volume: −12 to +12; relative preset volume.
Scale: Global, Off, Major, Minor, Harmonic Minor, Dorian, Mixolydian, Blues, or Pentatonic.
Root Note: C, C♯, D, D♯, E, F, F♯, G, G♯, A, A♯, or B.
Default Gate Length: 10–90; default 50, for sequencer and arpeggiator gates.
Seq 1–4 Smooth: Off or On for each sequencer modulation track.
Vocoder Hiss Mode: Off, Switched, or Pass; controls whether vocoder hiss is heard.
Vocoder Hiss Volume: −20 to 0; sets the vocoder hiss volume.
Global settings are available in both Utility and MIDI Control Center (MCC), except Reset Setting, which is available only in Utility.
Input Chan: All, 1–16, or None; MIDI receive channel.
Output Dest: None, USB, MIDI, or Both; where MIDI data is transmitted.
Local: Off or On; enables local editing with the knobs. Default: On.
Arp/Seq MIDI Out: Off or On; sends arpeggiator and sequencer data over MIDI.
Thru: Off or On; echoes MIDI In data to MIDI Out when On.
Knob Send CCs: Off or On; sends knob control-change data to external instruments.
Merge: USB+KBD, MIDI+KBD, or BOTH+KBD; chooses how keyboard data is merged into the MIDI stream.
Source: Internal, USB, MIDI, Clock, or Auto; chooses the tempo source.
Clock: One Step, 2 PPQ, 24 PPQ, or 48 PPQ; sets the clock standard.
Global Tempo: Off or On; when On, preset tempos are ignored and the most recently set tempo persists.
Pitch Format: 1 V/oct, Hz/V, or 1.2 V/oct; sets pitch CV output format.
Gate Format: S-Trig, V-Trig 5 V, or V-Trig 12 V; sets gate output format.
Pressure Range: 1–10 V; sets the Press output voltage range.
0 V Reference: C−1 to G8; sets the note that outputs zero volts in 1 V/oct or 1.2 V/oct format.
1 V Reference: C−1 to G8; sets the note that outputs one volt in Hz/V format.
Knob Catch: Jump, Hook, or Scaled; determines how a physical knob position meets its digital value.
Click to Load: Off or On; when On, loading a selected preset requires a click.
Osc Knob Speed: Slow or Fast; sets the response of the Wave, Timbre, and Shape knobs.
KBD Sensitivity: 10–100%; sets keyboard response for Pressure and Velocity.
Aftertouch Curve: Linear, Logarithmic, or Exponential.
Velocity Curve: Linear, Logarithmic, or Exponential.
Relative Bend: Off or On; when On, bending starts from where you touch the bend strip.
Scale: Off, Major, Minor, Harmonic Minor, Dorian, Mixolydian, Blues, or Pentatonic.
Root Note: C, C♯, D, D♯, E, F, F♯, G, G♯, A, A♯, or B.
Cent Offset: −50 to +50 cents from global tuning.
A Reference: 427.47–453.89 Hz; sets the frequency of A. The western tuning standard is 440 Hz.
Mic Gain: −12 dB to 59 dB, or Auto Gain; sets microphone gain for the vocoder.
Noise Gate: Off or −30 to −90 dB; sets the signal threshold.
Mic Detection: Off or On; when On, active sensing detects whether a microphone is present.
Mem Protect: Off permits overwriting all presets; Factory Only protects factory presets; On protects all presets.
Oct LED Blink: Off or On; sets whether active Octave Shift buttons glow steadily or blink.
Reset Setting: Cancel or Yes; restores factory settings, erases Utility changes, and erases presets. Available in Utility only.

MIDI Control Center (MCC) is an Arturia application for macOS and Windows. It transfers presets between the MicroFreak and a computer and changes MicroFreak settings. Download the latest version from Arturia.
The MCC manual covers features shared by Arturia products; this section covers MicroFreak-specific settings.
The Device tab contains MIDI and configuration settings for the MicroFreak.
Left column of MicroFreak Device Tab in MIDI Control Center
MIDI Input Channel: All, 1–16, or None. Sets the receive channel on the MicroFreak's 16-channel MIDI port.
MIDI Output Channel: 1–16. Sets the transmit channel.
MIDI Output Destination: Off, USB, MIDI, or MIDI + USB. USB connects directly to a computer; MIDI cables can run over longer distances.

Local control: With Local Off, the keyboard and panel controls send MIDI but do not directly play the MicroFreak. In a DAW, this lets the selected track route MIDI back to the MicroFreak or to another instrument. The MicroFreak can also play recorded MIDI while its keyboard controls another instrument.
Arp/Seq MIDI out: On or Off. Sends arpeggiator and sequencer notes to another instrument or a DAW.
MIDI through: When On, incoming MIDI echoes to MIDI Out.
Knob sends CCs: On or Off. Sends knob control-change data to external synths.
MIDI Merge: USB+KBD, MIDI+KBD, or BOTH+KBD. Chooses how keyboard data merges into the MIDI stream.
MIDI clock source: USB, MIDI, or Sync. USB is the built-in computer connection; MIDI uses the 5-pin DIN input.
Sync Clock In/Out settings: One Step, 2 PPQ, 24 PPQ, or 48 PPQ. The Sync port can connect to older, pre-MIDI devices such as Korg and Roland drum machines.
Global Tempo: When On, preset tempos are ignored and the most recently set tempo remains in use.
CV pitch format: 1 V/oct, Hz/V, or 1.2 V/oct. Sets the pitch CV output format; 1 V/oct is used by Eurorack, and 1.2 V/oct by Buchla.
CV Gate format: S-Trig, V-Trig 5 V, or V-Trig 12 V. Sets the Gate output format.
CV Press range: 1–10 V. Sets the Pressure output voltage range.
CV 0 V reference: C−1 to G8. Sets the note that outputs zero volts in volts-per-octave pitch formats.
CV 1 V reference: C−1 to G8. Sets the note that outputs one volt in Hz/V pitch format.

The Wavetables tab appears when MCC detects a connected MicroFreak. It loads custom wavetables for the User Wavetable oscillator type; it does not change other oscillator types, including the factory Wavetable Oscillator.
The left pane shows banks and wavetables on the computer; the right pane shows wavetables in the MicroFreak.
Below them, the information area shows the selected Bank and Wavetable names and a 3D animation of the wavetable. Click either name field to rename it.
The buttons above the computer and MicroFreak panes move and manage wavetables.
New Bank creates an empty bank on the computer and prompts for its name. Drag a wavetable over the new bank's name to add it; banks can combine wavetables from other banks.
Del Bank deletes a bank after confirmation. Factory banks cannot be deleted.
Replace Wavetable (.mfw) replaces the selected wavetable with a MicroFreak Wavetable file.
Replace Wavetable (.wav/.aiff) replaces it with a WAV or AIFF audio file.
Import New Bank imports an MFWB bank into the computer pane.
When importing WAV or AIFF audio, MicroFreak converts it into an MFW wavetable of 32 cycles, each 2,048 samples long:
Each group of 2,048 source samples counts as a cycle.
When importing WAV or AIFF audio, MicroFreak converts it into an MFW wavetable of 32 cycles, each 2,048 samples long:
The source's first and last cycles become cycles 1 and 32.
When importing WAV or AIFF audio, MicroFreak converts it into an MFW wavetable of 32 cycles, each 2,048 samples long:
With more than eight source cycles, MicroFreak distributes them evenly across the wavetable and crossfades between them.
When importing WAV or AIFF audio, MicroFreak converts it into an MFW wavetable of 32 cycles, each 2,048 samples long:
With fewer than eight source cycles, it spreads them across the slots so the Wave knob can reach every cycle.
When importing WAV or AIFF audio, MicroFreak converts it into an MFW wavetable of 32 cycles, each 2,048 samples long:
An audio file can therefore become a usable wavetable without manually preparing each cycle.
Export saves a selected wavetable as MFW or a selected bank as MFWB. Choose a location in the system save dialog.
Delete removes a selected wavetable after confirmation and replaces it with an init wavetable that morphs between simple waveforms.
Send to MicroFreak transfers the bank assembled in the computer pane to the MicroFreak for the User Wavetable oscillator.
Recall to Computer copies the MicroFreak's current wavetables into a new bank in the computer pane. The bank initially has a date-and-time name, which you can change in the Bank Name field.
Drag individual wavetables between the computer and MicroFreak in either direction. Shift-click or Command-click to select several before dragging.
A destination slot highlights blue when you hover over it. Releasing the wavetable there overwrites that slot.
Dragging a wavetable between computer and MicroFreak
Drag a wavetable within either pane to change its order. In the computer pane, drag a wavetable name over another bank's name to move it into that bank.
WAV and AIFF files can also be dragged from a file browser into either pane. Select several files with Shift-click or Command-click before dragging them together.

The Samples tab appears when MIDI Control Center detects a connected MicroFreak with current firmware. It loads user samples for the Sample oscillator and the Scan Grains, Cloud Grains, and Hit Grains oscillator types.
The left pane shows banks and samples on the computer; the right pane shows samples in the MicroFreak.

The information area shows the selected bank and sample names, sample length, total sample memory used, and remaining memory, with times displayed in seconds. Click a name field to rename the bank or sample.
The buttons above the panes manage samples on the computer and in the MicroFreak.
New Bank creates an empty bank on the computer and prompts for a name. Drag samples from other banks over the new bank's name to combine them.
Del Bank deletes a bank after confirmation. Factory banks cannot be deleted.
Replace Sample (.mfsz) replaces the selected sample with a MicroFreak Sample file.
Replace Sample (.wav/.aiff) replaces it with a WAV or AIFF audio file.
Import New Bank adds an MFSBZ bank to the computer pane.
Export saves the selected sample as MFSZ or the selected bank as MFSBZ. Choose a location in the system save dialog.
Delete removes a selected sample after confirmation and replaces it with an init sample.
Send to MicroFreak transfers the bank assembled in the computer pane to the MicroFreak for use by Sample, Scan Grains, Cloud Grains, and Hit Grains.
